Learners can multiply and divide integers and predict the sign of the answer
Learners can name and use closure, commutative, associative, identity and distributive properties
Learners can solve word problems involving temperature, depth, profit and loss

lessons.title: Integers, the number line, adding and subtracting

scenes.text: Asha reads the freezer: −18 °C. The kitchen is 27 °C.
"How many degrees warmer is the kitchen?" asks her brother.
She pictures a number line: from −18 up to 0 is 18 steps, then 27 more steps.
18 + 27 = 45. The kitchen is 45 °C warmer. Integers describe real life!

steps.title: What integers are
steps.body:
Integers are the numbers …, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, …

- Positive integers: 1, 2, 3, … (to the right of 0)
- Negative integers: −1, −2, −3, … (to the left of 0)
- 0 is neither positive nor negative.

On a number line, a number to the **right is always greater**. So −2 > −7 and 0 > −100.

steps.title: Rules for adding
steps.body:
- Same signs: add the sizes, keep the sign. (−6) + (−9) = −15
- Different signs: subtract the smaller size from the bigger, keep the sign of the bigger. (−11) + 4 = −7

On the number line: adding a positive number means move right, adding a negative number means move left.

steps.title: Subtracting = adding the additive inverse
steps.body:
To subtract an integer, add its opposite (additive inverse).

- a − b = a + (−b)
- 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8
- (−4) − 6 = (−4) + (−6) = −10

The additive inverse of 7 is −7; of −12 is 12. A number plus its inverse is 0.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Find (−25) + 18 − (−7).

- Step 1: (−25) + 18 = −7 (different signs: 25 − 18 = 7, bigger size is negative)
- Step 2: −7 − (−7) = −7 + 7 = 0
- Answer: **0**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
A submarine is at −120 m (120 m below sea level). It rises 45 m, then dives 70 m. Where is it now?

- Start: −120
- Rise 45: −120 + 45 = −75
- Dive 70: −75 + (−70) = −145
- Answer: **145 m below sea level (−145 m)**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Writing 5 − (−3) = 2. Two minus signs together become plus: the answer is 8.
- Thinking −8 is bigger than −3 because 8 > 3. On the number line −8 is further left, so −8 < −3.
- Forgetting the sign of the bigger number when signs differ: (−9) + 4 is −5, not 5.

statements.s: −15 is greater than −5.
statements.why: −15 lies to the left of −5 on the number line, so it is smaller.

statements.s: The additive inverse of −23 is 23.

statements.why: Same signs: add sizes and keep the minus: −10.

statements.s: 0 is a positive integer.

quiz.why: The signs differ, so subtract the sizes: 20 − 13 = 7. The bigger size, 20, is positive, so the answer is +7.
Subtracting −8 is the same as adding 8, so 12 − (−8) = 12 + 8 = 20.
On the number line, −9 is furthest left, so it is the smallest. Negative numbers with a bigger size are smaller.

quiz.q: The temperature was 5 °C and fell by 9 °C. New temperature?
quiz.why: A fall of 9 °C from 5 °C gives 5 + (−9) = −4 °C.
Subtracting 5 is adding −5, so (−7) − 5 = (−7) + (−5) = −12.

scenes.text: Ravi must add (−37) + 58 + 37 in his head.
He swaps the order: (−37) + 37 + 58.
(−37) + 37 = 0, so the answer is just 58. Properties make maths faster.

steps.title: Closure
steps.body:
The sum of two integers is always an integer, so integers are **closed under addition**. The difference of two integers is also always an integer, so they are **closed under subtraction** too.

Example: 7 − 15 = −8 (still an integer). Whole numbers are NOT closed under subtraction because 7 − 15 is not a whole number.

steps.title: Commutative and associative
steps.body:
- Commutative for addition: a + b = b + a. (−5) + 9 = 9 + (−5) = 4
- Associative for addition: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c)
- Subtraction is **not** commutative: 5 − 8 = −3 but 8 − 5 = 3
- Subtraction is **not** associative: (10 − 4) − 3 = 3 but 10 − (4 − 3) = 9

steps.title: Additive identity
steps.body: Adding 0 leaves an integer unchanged: a + 0 = 0 + a = a. So **0 is the additive identity**. Example: (−14) + 0 = −14.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Use properties to find (−46) + 89 + (−54).

- Group the negatives: [(−46) + (−54)] + 89 (commutative + associative)
- (−46) + (−54) = −100
- −100 + 89 = −11
- Answer: **−11**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
Show that subtraction is not commutative using −3 and 4.

- (−3) − 4 = −7
- 4 − (−3) = 7
- −7 ≠ 7, so a − b ≠ b − a in general.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Applying the commutative property to subtraction. You may swap only after rewriting as addition: 6 − 9 = 6 + (−9) = (−9) + 6.
- Saying 1 is the additive identity. 1 is the multiplicative identity; for addition it is 0.

activity.prompt: Match each statement to the property it shows.

quiz.q: Which operation on integers is NOT commutative?
quiz.why: Subtraction is not commutative, because the order changes the answer: 5 − 2 = 3, but 2 − 5 = −3. Addition is commutative.

quiz.q: The additive identity for integers is
quiz.why: The additive identity is 0, since a + 0 = a for any integer a.
Integers are closed under subtraction, because the difference of two integers is always an integer. For example, 3 − 7 = −4.

quiz.q: Which pair shows the associative property?
quiz.why: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c) is the associative property, since it is about grouping. a + b = b + a is commutative.
−125 and 125 cancel to give 0, so the sum is 68.

scenes.text: In a game Meena loses 4 coins each round.
After 3 rounds her change is 3 × (−4) = −12 coins.
"What was my coin change 3 rounds ago?" she wonders. Going back in time: (−3) × (−4) = +12. She had 12 more coins then!

steps.title: Sign rules for multiplication
steps.body:
- positive × positive = positive: 6 × 4 = 24
- positive × negative = negative: 6 × (−4) = −24
- negative × positive = negative: (−6) × 4 = −24
- negative × negative = positive: (−6) × (−4) = 24

Pattern behind the last rule: 3 × (−4) = −12, 2 × (−4) = −8, 1 × (−4) = −4, 0 × (−4) = 0. Each step adds 4, so (−1) × (−4) = 4.

steps.title: Many negative factors
steps.body:
Count the negative factors:

- **Even** number of negatives → product positive
- **Odd** number of negatives → product negative

So (−1)×(−1)×(−1) = −1 but (−1)×(−1)×(−1)×(−1) = 1. A zero factor makes the whole product 0.

steps.title: Properties of multiplication
steps.body:
- Closure: product of integers is an integer
- Commutative: a × b = b × a
- Associative: (a × b) × c = a × (b × c)
- Multiplicative identity: a × 1 = a
- Zero: a × 0 = 0
- Distributive: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c and a × (b − c) = a × b − a × c

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Find (−15) × 8 × (−2).

- Two negative factors → product positive
- 15 × 8 × 2 = 15 × 16 = 240
- Answer: **240**

steps.title: Solved example 3 (word problem)
steps.body:
In a test, +3 marks for a correct answer and −1 for a wrong one. Riya gets 12 correct and 8 wrong. Her score?

- Correct: 12 × 3 = 36
- Wrong: 8 × (−1) = −8
- Total: 36 + (−8) = **28 marks**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- (−3) × (−5) = −15 is wrong; two negatives give +15.
- (−2)⁴ vs −2⁴: (−2)×(−2)×(−2)×(−2) = 16, while −2⁴ means −(2⁴) = −16.
- Forgetting to multiply the sign along with the number in distributive steps.

activity.prompt: Sort each product by its sign.

quiz.why: A negative times a negative is positive, so (−9) × (−7) = 63.

quiz.q: The product of 5 negative integers is
quiz.why: A product of an odd number of negative integers is negative. With 5 negatives, the product is negative.
Multiplying by −1 gives the additive inverse (the opposite), so (−1) × 57 = −57.
The multiplicative identity is 1, since a × 1 = a.

quiz.q: A lift goes down 6 m every minute. Change in height after 7 minutes?
quiz.why: Going down 6 m each minute for 7 minutes is 7 × (−6) = −42 m.

lessons.title: Dividing integers and solving word problems

scenes.text: Four friends ran a lemonade stall and made a loss of ₹200.
They share it equally: (−200) ÷ 4 = −50.
Each friend records −₹50: a loss of ₹50 each.

steps.title: Sign rules for division
steps.body:
Division follows the same sign rules as multiplication:

- (+) ÷ (+) = +, (−) ÷ (−) = +
- (+) ÷ (−) = −, (−) ÷ (+) = −

Examples: (−48) ÷ 8 = −6; (−48) ÷ (−8) = 6; 48 ÷ (−8) = −6.

steps.title: Properties of division
steps.body:
- Integers are **not closed** under division: (−5) ÷ 2 is not an integer.
- Division is **not commutative**: 12 ÷ (−4) = −3 but (−4) ÷ 12 is not −3.
- a ÷ 1 = a and a ÷ (−1) = −a
- 0 ÷ a = 0 for any non-zero a
- **a ÷ 0 is not defined.** No number times 0 gives a non-zero a.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
The temperature falls at a steady 2 °C per hour from 10 °C at midnight. When will it be −8 °C?

- Total fall needed: 10 − (−8) = 18 °C
- Hours: 18 ÷ 2 = 9
- Answer: **9 a.m.**

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
Find an integer that makes (−32) ÷ ___ = 4 true.

- We need x with (−32) ÷ x = 4, so x = (−32) ÷ 4 = −8
- Check: (−32) ÷ (−8) = 4 ✓
- Answer: **−8**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Writing 0 ÷ 0 = 0 or 7 ÷ 0 = 0. Division by zero is undefined.
- Forgetting that (−a) ÷ (−b) is positive.
- In word problems, using the wrong sign for 'below', 'loss', 'fall' (these are negative).

activity.prompt: A diver goes from 0 m to −60 m in equal steps of −5 m. How many steps does she take?

quiz.why: Negative ÷ negative is positive, so (−84) ÷ (−12) = 84 ÷ 12 = 7.
Division by zero is not defined, so 9 ÷ 0 has no value. The others are fine.
Different signs give a negative result, so (−75) ÷ 25 = −3.
Integers are not closed under division, since the result may not be an integer. For example, 7 ÷ 2 = 3.5.

quiz.q: A shopkeeper has a loss of ₹15 per pen. Total loss −₹285. How many pens?
quiz.why: Total loss ÷ loss per pen = (−285) ÷ (−15) = 19 pens.

questions.q: Which integer is greater: −12 or −21?
questions.why: −12 is to the right of −21 on the number line, so −12 is greater.
A number plus its additive inverse is 0, so (−17) + 17 = 0.
A negative times a negative is positive, so (−6) × (−6) = 36.

questions.q: Additive inverse of −45 is
questions.why: The additive inverse of −45 is 45, because −45 + 45 = 0.
Subtracting −15 is adding 15: (−40) + 15 = −25.

questions.q: The value of (−1)⁵ × (−1)⁶ is
questions.why: (−1)⁵ = −1, since 5 is odd, and (−1)⁶ = 1, since 6 is even. So the product is −1 × 1 = −1.
The equation shows multiplication spreading over addition, which is the distributive property.
(−144) ÷ 12 = −12, and (−12) ÷ (−3) = 4, since two negatives give a positive.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Integers are closed under subtraction. Reason (R): The difference of any two integers is an integer.
options: Both true, R does not explain A
questions.why: Both are true: the difference of any two integers is an integer, which is why integers are closed under subtraction. The reason explains the assertion.

questions.q: Assertion (A): a ÷ 0 = 0 for any integer a. Reason (R): 0 ÷ a = 0 for non-zero a.
options: Both true, R does not explain A
questions.why: The assertion is false: dividing by 0 is undefined, so a ÷ 0 = 0 is wrong. The reason is true, since 0 ÷ a = 0 for non-zero a.

questions.q: Evaluate 25 × (−37) × 4 smartly.
Case: A quiz gives +5 for correct, −2 for incorrect. Kiran answered 20 questions and scored 30. If all attempted, how many were correct?
questions.why: Let c be the correct answers. Then 5c − 2(20 − c) = 30, so 7c − 40 = 30 and c = 10.

questions.q: Case: Mount Everest summit is about 8848 m above sea level; a trench point is 10 994 m below. Height difference?
questions.why: The height difference is 8848 − (−10 994) = 8848 + 10 994 = 19 842 m.

questions.q: A cement company earns ₹8 profit per bag of white cement and loses ₹5 per bag of grey cement. It sells 3000 white and 5000 grey bags. Net result?
The temperature drops 3 °C every hour from 12 °C. After how many hours will it first be below −9 °C?
questions.why: After 7 hours the temperature is 12 − 21 = −9 °C, which is not below −9. After 8 hours it is −12 °C, so it first goes below −9 °C after 8 hours.

questions.q: If a × b = −56 and a ÷ b = −14, where a is a positive integer, then

courses.title: Ch 2 · Fractions and Decimals
courses.summary: Multiplying and dividing fractions and decimals, reciprocals, "of" as multiplication, shifting the decimal point by powers of 10, and everyday measurement problems.
outcomes: Learners can multiply a fraction by a whole number and by another fraction
Learners can divide using reciprocals
Learners can multiply and divide decimals, including by 10, 100 and 1000
Learners can solve word problems with money, length and weight

story.title: Half of three-quarters of a cake

scenes.text: Three-quarters of a cake is left after a party.
Neha eats half of what is left. What part of the whole cake is that?
½ of ¾ = ½ × ¾ = 3/8 of the cake.

steps.title: Fraction × whole number
steps.body:
Multiply the numerator by the whole number; keep the denominator.

- 3 × 2/7 = 6/7
- 4 × 5/6 = 20/6 = 10/3 = 3⅓

For mixed numbers, first convert: 2 × 1¾ = 2 × 7/4 = 14/4 = 3½.

steps.title: "of" means multiply
steps.body: ¼ of 20 = ¼ × 20 = 5. ⅔ of 18 = 12. Whenever you read 'fraction of a quantity', multiply.

steps.title: Fraction × fraction
steps.body:
Product = (product of numerators) / (product of denominators).

- 2/3 × 4/5 = 8/15
- Cancel common factors first to keep numbers small: 6/7 × 14/9 = (6×14)/(7×9) → cancel 7 and 3 → 4/3

When you multiply two proper fractions, the product is **smaller** than each of them. Multiplying by an improper fraction makes the number bigger.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
A car runs 16 km on 1 litre of petrol. How far on 2¾ litres?

- Distance = 16 × 2¾ = 16 × 11/4
- = 4 × 11 = 44
- Answer: **44 km**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Multiplying a whole number into both numerator and denominator: 3 × 2/7 is 6/7, not 6/21.
- Multiplying mixed numbers part by part: 2½ × 1½ is NOT 2 + ¼. Convert to improper fractions first: 5/2 × 3/2 = 15/4.
- Forgetting to simplify the final answer.

activity.prompt: Match each product with its value.

quiz.why: Multiply the numerators and the denominators: (1 × 1)/(2 × 3) = 1/6.

quiz.q: Product of two proper fractions is
quiz.why: Each proper fraction is less than 1, so multiplying them gives a number smaller than each of them.

scenes.text: Pooja has 6 m of ribbon. Each bow needs ¾ m.
How many bows? She needs 6 ÷ ¾.
Flip and multiply: 6 × 4/3 = 8 bows.

steps.title: Reciprocal
steps.body:
Two numbers whose product is 1 are reciprocals. The reciprocal of a/b is b/a (a, b ≠ 0).

- Reciprocal of 5/9 is 9/5
- Reciprocal of 7 is 1/7
- 0 has no reciprocal.

steps.title: Dividing
steps.body:
To divide by a fraction, **multiply by its reciprocal**.

- Whole ÷ fraction: 6 ÷ ¾ = 6 × 4/3 = 8
- Fraction ÷ whole: ⅔ ÷ 4 = ⅔ × ¼ = 1/6
- Fraction ÷ fraction: ⅝ ÷ 5/12 = ⅝ × 12/5 = 12/8 = 3/2

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
A 31½ litre water tank fills jugs of 1¾ litres each. How many jugs?

- 31½ = 63/2, 1¾ = 7/4
- 63/2 ÷ 7/4 = 63/2 × 4/7 = 9 × 2 = 18
- Answer: **18 jugs**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Flipping the wrong fraction: in a ÷ b only the divisor b is flipped.
- Flipping before converting a mixed number: change 2½ to 5/2 first, then flip to 2/5.
- Thinking division always makes things smaller: dividing by a proper fraction makes the answer bigger (6 ÷ ½ = 12).

activity.prompt: Fill in the reciprocals and answers.

quiz.why: The reciprocal of 1/8 is 8, because 1/8 × 8 = 1.
Dividing by ⅓ is multiplying by 3, so 9 ÷ ⅓ = 9 × 3 = 27.
Dividing by 5 is multiplying by ⅕, so ⅚ × ⅕ = 5/30 = 1/6.
Zero has no reciprocal, since no number multiplied by 0 gives 1.
2¼ = 9/4. Dividing by ¾ is multiplying by 4/3, so 9/4 × 4/3 = 3.

scenes.text: Petrol costs ₹104.50 a litre. Dad buys 2.4 litres for the scooter.
104.50 × 2.4: multiply 10450 × 24 = 250 800, then count decimal places (2 + 1 = 3).
250.800 → ₹250.80. The pump display agrees!

steps.title: By 10, 100, 1000
steps.body:
Multiplying by 10, 100, 1000 moves the decimal point **right** by 1, 2, 3 places.

- 3.27 × 10 = 32.7
- 3.27 × 100 = 327
- 3.27 × 1000 = 3270 (add a zero as needed)

steps.title: Decimal × decimal
steps.body:
1. Ignore the points and multiply as whole numbers.
2. Count decimal places in both factors together.
3. Put that many decimal places in the product.

Example: 1.5 × 0.04 → 15 × 4 = 60; places 1 + 2 = 3 → 0.060 = 0.06.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Find the area of a rectangle 6.2 cm × 4.5 cm.

- 62 × 45 = 2790
- Decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2 → 27.90
- Area = **27.9 cm²**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
A bus travels 0.85 km in a minute. Distance in 40 minutes?

- 0.85 × 40 = 85 × 40 ÷ 100 = 3400 ÷ 100
- = **34 km**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Lining up decimal points as in addition. In multiplication you count places instead.
- 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.9 is wrong: 3 × 3 = 9 with 2 places → 0.09.
- Dropping needed zeros: 0.02 × 0.4 = 0.008, not 0.08.

activity.prompt: Compute 2.5 × 0.12

quiz.why: Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point 2 places right, so 0.07 × 100 = 7.
12 × 5 = 60, and there are 2 decimal places in total, so 1.2 × 0.5 = 0.60 = 0.6.
4 × 4 = 16, and there are 2 decimal places, so 0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16.

quiz.q: Cost of 3.5 kg apples at ₹120 per kg?

quiz.why: 2.31 has 2 decimal places and 0.004 has 3, so the product has 2 + 3 = 5 decimal places.

scenes.text: A tailor has 7.5 m of cloth to cut into pieces 0.25 m long.
7.5 ÷ 0.25: make the divisor a whole number by multiplying both by 100.

steps.title: Decimal ÷ whole number
steps.body:
Divide as usual and place the point in the quotient directly above the point in the dividend.

- 8.4 ÷ 4 = 2.1
- 0.65 ÷ 5 = 0.13

steps.title: Decimal ÷ decimal
steps.body:
Multiply divisor and dividend by the same power of 10 so the divisor becomes a whole number, then divide.

- 2.88 ÷ 0.9 = 28.8 ÷ 9 = 3.2
- 0.144 ÷ 0.12 = 14.4 ÷ 12 = 1.2

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
A car covers 89.1 km in 2.2 hours. Average distance per hour?

- 89.1 ÷ 2.2 = 891 ÷ 22
- 22 × 40 = 880, remainder 11, 11/22 = 0.5
- Answer: **40.5 km per hour**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Multiplying only the divisor by 10 and forgetting the dividend.
- Placing the point wrongly: 0.65 ÷ 5 is 0.13, not 1.3.
- Thinking the answer must be smaller than the dividend; dividing by a decimal less than 1 gives a bigger answer.

activity.prompt: Match each division to its answer.

quiz.why: Dividing by 100 moves the decimal point 2 places left, so 72.5 ÷ 100 = 0.725.
Multiply both numbers by 10: 42 ÷ 7 = 6.
108 ÷ 9 = 12, and since 1.08 has 2 decimal places, 1.08 ÷ 9 = 0.12.

quiz.q: Price of 1 pen if 12 pens cost ₹102?
quiz.why: One pen costs ₹102 ÷ 12 = ₹8.50.
Multiply both numbers by 100: 50 ÷ 5 = 10.

questions.q: Reciprocal of 9/4 is
questions.why: The reciprocal of 9/4 is 4/9, by flipping the fraction.
Multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point one place right, so 0.5 × 10 = 5.

questions.q: ⅖ ÷ ⅘ = ?
questions.why: Dividing by 4/5 is multiplying by 5/4, so ⅖ × 5/4 = 10/20 = ½.
25 × 4 = 100, and there are 3 decimal places in total, so 2.5 × 0.04 = 0.100 = 0.1.
Multiply both numbers by 10: 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

questions.q: Which is greater: ⅔ of 27 or ¾ of 24?
questions.why: ⅔ of 27 = 18 and ¾ of 24 = 18, so the two are equal.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 5 ÷ ½ = 10. Reason (R): Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal.
options: Both true, R does not explain A
questions.why: Both are true: dividing by ½ is multiplying by 2, so 5 ÷ ½ = 5 × 2 = 10. The reason explains the assertion.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 0.2 × 0.3 = 0.6. Reason (R): 2 × 3 = 6.
questions.why: The assertion is false: 0.2 × 0.3 = 0.06, as the product has two decimal places. The reason, 2 × 3 = 6, is true but only part of the working.

questions.q: Side of a square is 2.5 cm. Its area is
questions.why: The area of a square is side × side = 2.5 × 2.5 = 6.25 cm².

questions.q: Case: A ¾ litre bottle of juice is shared equally among 6 children. How much does each get?
questions.why: Each child gets ¾ ÷ 6 = ¾ × 1/6 = 3/24 = ⅛ litre.

questions.q: Case: Cloth costs ₹48.75 per metre. Cost of 4.2 m?
questions.why: Cost = 48.75 × 4.2 = 204.75, so the cloth costs ₹204.75.

questions.q: A road 4.8 km long is divided into equal parts of 0.16 km. Number of parts?
In a 24-hour day, Pratap studies for 5/12 of the day and Vidya for ⅓ of the day. How many more hours does Pratap study?
questions.why: Pratap studies 5/12 of 24 = 10 hours, and Vidya studies ⅓ of 24 = 8 hours. The difference is 2 hours.

questions.q: A tank is ⅗ full. After 21 litres are used it is ¼ full. Capacity of the tank?
questions.why: The tank goes from ⅗ full to ¼ full, so the 21 L used is ⅗ − ¼ = 7/20 of the capacity. Capacity = 21 × 20/7 = 60 L.

courses.title: Ch 3 · Data Handling
courses.summary: Organising data and finding a single value that represents it — mean, median, mode and range — then reading and drawing bar and double bar graphs, and a first look at chance and probability.
outcomes: Learners can find the arithmetic mean and range of a data set
Learners can find the mode and median and choose the best representative value
Learners can read and draw bar graphs and double bar graphs with a sensible scale
Learners can describe events as certain, impossible or possible and find simple probabilities

scenes.text: Arjun scored 30, 45, 0, 60, 15 in five matches; Sameer scored 30, 28, 32, 31, 29.
Both averages: Arjun 150 ÷ 5 = 30, Sameer 150 ÷ 5 = 30. Same mean!
But Arjun's range is 60 − 0 = 60; Sameer's is 32 − 28 = 4. Sameer is far more consistent.

steps.title: Representative values
steps.body: When we have a lot of data we want one number that tells us 'roughly what is typical'. Such a number is a **representative value** or measure of central tendency. Class 7 uses three: **mean, median, mode**.

steps.title: Arithmetic mean
steps.body:
Mean (average) = (sum of all observations) ÷ (number of observations).

The mean always lies between the smallest and the largest value. It is affected by every value, including extreme ones.

steps.title: Range
steps.body: Range = highest observation − lowest observation. It shows how spread out the data is.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Ages of 6 cousins: 4, 7, 9, 12, 13, 15. Find the mean and range.

- Sum = 4 + 7 + 9 + 12 + 13 + 15 = 60
- Mean = 60 ÷ 6 = **10 years**
- Range = 15 − 4 = **11 years**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
The mean of 5 numbers is 18. Four of them are 12, 20, 15, 25. Find the fifth.

- Total of all 5 = 5 × 18 = 90
- Known sum = 12 + 20 + 15 + 25 = 72
- Fifth = 90 − 72 = **18**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Dividing by the wrong count (e.g. forgetting a 0 observation — zeros still count!).
- Range = highest − lowest, not highest + lowest, and not 'first minus last'.
- Thinking the mean must be one of the data values. It need not be.

activity.prompt: Rainfall (mm) on 5 days: 0, 12, 8, 20, 10. Find the mean rainfall.

quiz.why: The mean is the sum divided by the number of values: (2 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 10) ÷ 5 = 30 ÷ 5 = 6.
Range = largest − smallest = 45 − 7 = 38.

quiz.q: The mean of first five whole numbers (0 to 4) is
quiz.why: The first five whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Their mean is 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

quiz.q: Mean of 8 numbers is 20. Their sum is
quiz.why: Sum = mean × number of values = 8 × 20 = 160.

quiz.q: Which is always between the smallest and largest value?
quiz.why: The mean always lies between the smallest and largest values. The range and sum do not lie in that interval.

scenes.text: A shop must stock school shoes. Sizes sold last week: 5, 6, 6, 7, 6, 8, 5, 6, 7.
The average size 6.2 is not a real shoe size!
Size 6 appears most often (4 times) — the mode. That is what the shopkeeper should stock most.

steps.title: Mode
steps.body:
The **mode** is the observation that occurs most often. A data set may have one mode, more than one mode, or (if all appear equally) no useful mode.

For large data, make a frequency table first.

steps.title: Median
steps.body:
The **median** is the middle value after arranging the data in order.

- Odd number of observations n: median is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th value.
- Even number: median is the mean of the two middle values (Class 7 mainly uses odd counts).

The median splits the data into two equal halves and is not pulled by an extreme value.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Find the mode and median of 14, 25, 14, 28, 18, 17, 18, 14, 23, 22, 14, 18.

- Arrange: 14, 14, 14, 14, 17, 18, 18, 18, 22, 23, 25, 28
- Mode: 14 occurs 4 times → **14**
- 12 values: middle two are the 6th and 7th = 18 and 18 → median **18**

steps.title: Which value to use?
steps.body:
- Mean: when values are fairly even (marks, temperatures).
- Median: when there are extreme values (incomes, house prices).
- Mode: for 'most popular' questions (shoe size, favourite colour).

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Taking the middle value without arranging the data first.
- Giving the frequency (4) as the mode instead of the value (14).
- Forgetting that a data set can have two modes.

activity.prompt: Which representative value suits each situation best?

items.text: Typical salary when one person earns crores
Average marks of a class test
Size of school uniform to order most
Average daily temperature in a week
Middle house price in a street with one palace

quiz.why: The mode is the value that occurs most often. 3 appears three times, more than any other.
Order the data: 2, 4, 5, 7, 9. The middle value is 5, so the median is 5.

quiz.q: Which is least affected by one very large value?
quiz.why: The median depends on the middle position, not on size, so one very large value hardly changes it. The mean is pulled by extremes.
In 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, both 1 and 2 appear twice, so there are two modes.
With an even number of values, the median is the mean of the middle two: (20 + 30) ÷ 2 = 25.

lessons.title: Bar graphs and double bar graphs

scenes.text: The PE teacher wants to compare how many students joined each sport in 2024 and 2025.
She draws pairs of bars side by side — one colour per year — for each sport.
At a glance everyone sees kabaddi doubled while chess stayed the same.

steps.title: Bar graph
steps.body:
A bar graph shows data with bars of **equal width** and **equal gaps**. Bar lengths are proportional to the values. Choose a **scale** (e.g. 1 unit = 10 students) so that the biggest bar fits.

Always label both axes and give a title.

steps.title: Double bar graph
steps.body: A double bar graph places two bars side by side for each category to **compare two sets of data** (two years, boys vs girls, two classes). A key (legend) shows which colour is which.

steps.title: Solved example 1: choosing a scale
steps.body:
Books sold: Mon 120, Tue 250, Wed 180, Thu 300. Suitable scale?

- Largest value 300; with 1 unit = 50 books the tallest bar is 6 units — easy to draw.
- Bar heights: 2.4, 5, 3.6, 6 units.

steps.title: Solved example 2: reading a double bar graph
steps.body:
A double bar graph shows marks: Maths (Term 1: 60, Term 2: 75), Science (70, 68), English (55, 72).

- Biggest improvement: English (+17)
- Subject that went down: Science (−2)
- Term 2 total = 75 + 68 + 72 = 215

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Bars of different widths or uneven gaps.
- Scale that does not start at 0, making differences look bigger than they are.
- Missing the key in a double bar graph.

activity.prompt: Put the steps for drawing a bar graph in order.
items: Collect and tabulate the data
Draw and label the two axes
Choose a suitable scale
Draw bars of equal width with equal gaps
Give the graph a title (and key if double bar)

quiz.q: In a bar graph, bar width should be
quiz.why: In a bar graph, the bars should be of equal width, so only the length shows the value. Different widths would mislead.

quiz.q: A double bar graph is used to
quiz.why: A double bar graph compares two sets of data, with two bars for each category.

quiz.q: Scale 1 unit = 20 kg. A bar 3.5 units long shows
quiz.why: A bar of 3.5 units with 1 unit = 20 kg shows 3.5 × 20 = 70 kg.

quiz.q: Largest value 840. Which scale is most convenient?
quiz.why: For a largest value of 840, a scale of 1 unit = 100 gives 8.4 units, which is a good size. 1 unit = 1 would be far too long.

quiz.q: What tells you which colour is which year?
quiz.why: The key (legend) tells which colour stands for which year or group.

scenes.text: The captains toss a coin. Kabir calls heads.
There are 2 equally likely outcomes: heads or tails.
So the probability of heads is 1 out of 2 = ½.

steps.title: Certain, impossible, maybe
steps.body:
- **Certain**: will surely happen (the sun rises in the east).
- **Impossible**: can never happen (rolling a 7 on a normal die).
- **Possible / may happen**: rain tomorrow, getting a 6 on a die.

steps.title: Probability of an event
steps.body:
For equally likely outcomes:

Probability = (number of favourable outcomes) ÷ (total number of outcomes).

- A coin: P(head) = 1/2
- A die: P(getting 4) = 1/6; P(even number) = 3/6 = 1/2

Probability is between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain).

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. One ball is drawn without looking. P(red)?

- Total balls = 10
- Favourable (red) = 4
- P(red) = 4/10 = **2/5**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
A die is thrown. Find P(number greater than 4).

- Outcomes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 (6 outcomes)
- Greater than 4: 5, 6 (2 outcomes)
- P = 2/6 = **1/3**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Thinking 'it has not come for a long time, so it must come next'. Each toss is independent.
- Writing a probability greater than 1.
- Forgetting to count all outcomes (e.g. counting a die as 5 outcomes).

bands.text: About even chance, like a coin toss.
Likely — expect it most of the time.

quiz.q: P(tail) when tossing a fair coin is
quiz.why: A fair coin has 2 equally likely outcomes, and 1 is a tail, so P(tail) = 1/2.
A die has only 1 to 6, so getting 7 is impossible. Its probability is 0.

quiz.q: A spinner has 8 equal parts, 3 green. P(green) =
quiz.why: 3 of the 8 equal parts are green, so P(green) = 3/8.
The odd numbers on a die are 1, 3 and 5, so P(odd) = 3/6 = 1/2.
A probability must be between 0 and 1. Only 0.75 is in that range, while 1.4, 5/4 and −0.2 are not.

questions.q: Mean of 5, 10, 15 is
Mode of 4, 6, 4, 8, 4, 6 is
questions.why: The mode is the most frequent value. 4 appears 3 times and 6 appears 2 times, so the mode is 4.

questions.q: Range of 12, 3, 27, 18 is
Median of 31, 18, 25, 40, 22 is
questions.why: Ordered, the data is 18, 22, 25, 31, 40. The middle value is 25.

questions.q: P(a vowel) if a letter is picked from the word MATHS?
questions.why: The word MATHS has 5 letters and only A is a vowel, so P(vowel) = 1/5.

questions.q: Mean of 10 observations is 15. If each is increased by 3, the new mean is
questions.why: Adding 3 to every observation adds 3 to the mean, so the new mean is 15 + 3 = 18.

questions.q: Which representative value is best for "most common shoe size"?
questions.why: The most common shoe size is the value that occurs most often, so the mode is the best measure.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Mean of 2, 4, 6, 100 is a good typical value. Reason (R): Mean is affected by extreme values.
questions.why: The assertion is false: the mean of 2, 4, 6, 100 is 28, which is not typical because 100 pulls it up. The reason is true, as the mean is affected by extremes.

questions.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 12; one number, 22, is removed. New mean of the 5 numbers?
questions.why: The total of the 6 numbers is 6 × 12 = 72. After removing 22, the sum is 50 for 5 numbers, so the new mean is 10.

questions.q: Marks: 40, 55, 70, x, 60. Mean is 56. x =
questions.why: The total is 5 × 56 = 280. The known marks add to 40 + 55 + 70 + 60 = 225, so x = 280 − 225 = 55.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red, 5 green and 2 yellow balls. P(not green)?
questions.why: There are 3 + 5 + 2 = 10 balls and 5 are not green, so P(not green) = 5/10 = 1/2.

questions.q: Case: A double bar graph shows girls/boys in clubs: Art (12, 8), Music (9, 15), Science (14, 14). Which club has the greatest total?
questions.why: Art has 12 + 8 = 20, Music 9 + 15 = 24 and Science 14 + 14 = 28. So Science has the greatest total.

questions.q: Case (same graph): In which club do boys outnumber girls by the most?
questions.why: Boys minus girls: Art 8 − 12 = −4, Music 15 − 9 = 6 and Science 0. Music has boys ahead by the most, 6.

questions.q: Median of the first 9 odd numbers is
questions.why: The first 9 odd numbers are 1, 3, 5, …, 17. The 5th value, the middle one, is 9.

questions.q: Mean of 5 numbers is 27. If one number is excluded, the mean becomes 25. The excluded number is
questions.why: The sum of the 5 numbers is 5 × 27 = 135. After excluding one, the sum of 4 is 4 × 25 = 100, so the excluded number is 135 − 100 = 35.

questions.q: Data: 3, 7, 7, 9, x. If mode is 7 and mean is 7, x =
questions.why: The mean is 7, so the sum is 35, giving 3 + 7 + 7 + 9 + x = 35, so x = 9. Then 7 appears twice, so it is still the mode.

courses.title: Ch 4 · Simple Equations
courses.summary: What an equation is, solving it with the balance method and by transposing, building equations from a solution, and turning word problems into equations.
outcomes: Learners can write an equation from a statement
Learners can solve one-variable linear equations by balancing and transposing, and check the answer
Learners can form many equations with a given solution
Learners can solve practical word problems using equations

scenes.text: "Think of a number, multiply it by 4, add 5. Tell me the result." Raju says 65.
Ameena writes 4x + 5 = 65 and quickly finds x = 15.
Raju is amazed. Ameena explains: it is just a simple equation.

steps.title: Equation = condition on a variable
steps.body:
An **equation** is a statement that two expressions are equal, with a variable (letter) for an unknown number. It has a **left-hand side (LHS)**, an equals sign and a **right-hand side (RHS)**.

- 4x + 5 = 65 is an equation.
- 4x + 5 > 65 is not an equation (no equals sign).
- 4 + 5 = 9 is a numerical statement, with no variable.

steps.title: Solution
steps.body: The value of the variable that makes LHS = RHS is the **solution** (root). Try values: for x + 3 = 7, x = 4 works because 4 + 3 = 7. Trial and error works for small numbers but becomes slow — we need systematic methods.

steps.title: Solved example 1: statement → equation
steps.body:
- 'Seven times a number minus 4 is 31' → 7m − 4 = 31
- 'One-third of a number plus 5 is 8' → x/3 + 5 = 8
- 'Rahul's age is 5 more than twice Sita's (s); Rahul is 23' → 2s + 5 = 23

steps.title: Solved example 2: equation → statement
steps.body:
- 3p = 15 → 'Three times p is 15.'
- y/4 − 2 = 6 → 'Two less than one-fourth of y is 6.'

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Writing 'four less than x' as 4 − x. It is x − 4.
- Treating 2x = 10 as x = 10 − 2. 2x means 2 × x.

activity.prompt: Match the statement to its equation.

quiz.why: An equation has an equals sign and a variable, as x + 4 = 9 does. 'x + 4 > 9' is an inequality and 'x + 4' is an expression.
x − 5 = 3 gives x = 3 + 5 = 8. Check: 8 − 5 = 3.
'Five times a number is 40' means 5 × x = 40, written 5x = 40.
Put x = 3 into 2x + 1: 2(3) + 1 = 7, which matches the right side. So yes, it is a solution.
'Four less than m' means m − 4, so the equation is m − 4 = 11.

scenes.text: Grandma puts a bag of rice (x kg) and a 2 kg weight on one pan; 7 kg on the other. They balance.
Remove 2 kg from both pans — still balanced: x = 5.
Whatever you do to one side, do to the other.

steps.title: Balance method
steps.body:
An equation is like a balanced scale. You may:

- add the same number to both sides
- subtract the same number from both sides
- multiply both sides by the same number
- divide both sides by the same non-zero number

The balance (equality) is kept.

steps.title: Transposing
steps.body:
Moving a term to the other side changes its operation to the opposite:

- + becomes −, − becomes +
- × becomes ÷, ÷ becomes ×

x + 5 = 12 → x = 12 − 5 = 7. 3y = 18 → y = 18 ÷ 3 = 6. This is a shortcut of the balance method.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Solve 3n + 7 = 25.

- Subtract 7: 3n = 18
- Divide by 3: n = 6
- Check: 3(6) + 7 = 25 ✓

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
Solve y/5 − 2 = 4.

- Add 2: y/5 = 6
- Multiply by 5: y = 30

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Transposing without changing the sign: x + 5 = 12 → x = 12 + 5 (wrong).
- Dividing only one term: 3n + 7 = 25 → n + 7 = 25/3 (wrong). Remove the 7 first, or divide every term.
- Not checking the answer by substituting.

activity.prompt: Solve 5x − 8 = 27. x = ?

quiz.q: First step to solve 7 − 2a = 1 by transposing
quiz.why: Transposing +7 to the right side changes it to −7, so −2a = 1 − 7.

story.title: Make a puzzle for your friend

scenes.text: Tanvi wants a puzzle whose answer is 4.
Start with x = 4, multiply by 3: 3x = 12, then add 5: 3x + 5 = 17.
Her friend solves 3x + 5 = 17 and gets 4. Endless puzzles from one answer!

steps.title: Building equations
steps.body:
Start with the solution, e.g. x = 5, and do the same operation to both sides as many times as you like:

- ×2: 2x = 10
- −3: 2x − 3 = 7
- ÷4 instead: x/4 = 5/4

Every equation built this way has the same solution, x = 5.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Make two equations with solution y = −2.

- y = −2 → ×5 → 5y = −10 → +12 → **5y + 12 = 2**
- y = −2 → −1 → **y − 1 = −3**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
Make an equation with solution m = 3/2.

- m = 3/2 → ×2 → 2m = 3 → +1 → **2m + 1 = 4**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Doing an operation to only one side, which changes the solution.
- Multiplying by 0: 0 × x = 0 is true for every x, so it loses the solution.

statements.s: 2x + 1 = 11 has solution x = 5.
x/2 = 6 has solution x = 3.
3y − 4 = 5 and y = 3 are equivalent.
Multiplying both sides by 0 keeps the solution.

quiz.why: For x + 4 = 6, x = 2, because 2 + 4 = 6. The other equations do not give x = 2.

quiz.q: Starting with p = 4, multiply by 3 then subtract 2. Equation?
quiz.why: Starting from p = 4, multiplying by 3 gives 12, and subtracting 2 gives 10. So the equation is 3p − 2 = 10.

quiz.q: Which does NOT have solution y = −1?
quiz.why: Putting y = −1 into 4y + 1 gives −3, not 3. The other equations are all true for y = −1.

quiz.q: How many equations can have the solution x = 7?
quiz.why: Infinitely many equations have x = 7 as their solution, since we can keep forming new ones such as x + 1 = 8.

quiz.q: From z = 6, dividing both sides by 3 then adding 1 gives
quiz.why: From z = 6, dividing by 3 gives z/3 = 2, and adding 1 gives z/3 + 1 = 3.

scenes.text: Class 7A planted some saplings; 7B planted 15 more than 7A. Together 95 saplings.
Let 7A plant x. Then 7B planted x + 15. Equation: x + (x + 15) = 95.
2x = 80, x = 40. 7A planted 40 and 7B planted 55.

steps.title: A five-step method
steps.body:
1. Read and decide the unknown; call it x.
2. Write other quantities in terms of x.
3. Form the equation from the condition.
4. Solve it.
5. Check in the original words and answer in a sentence with units.

steps.title: Solved example 1 (ages)
steps.body:
Raju's father's age is 5 years more than three times Raju's age. Father is 44. Raju's age?

- Let Raju = y years
- 3y + 5 = 44
- 3y = 39, y = 13
- **Raju is 13 years old.** Check: 3 × 13 + 5 = 44 ✓

steps.title: Solved example 2 (geometry)
steps.body:
The length of a rectangle is 3 cm more than its breadth. Perimeter is 34 cm. Find the sides.

- Breadth = b, length = b + 3
- 2(b + b + 3) = 34 → 2b + 3 = 17 → b = 7
- **Breadth 7 cm, length 10 cm**

steps.title: Solved example 3 (money)
steps.body:
Irfan has ₹7 more than twice what Parmit has. Irfan has ₹37. How much does Parmit have?

- 2p + 7 = 37 → 2p = 30 → p = 15
- **Parmit has ₹15.**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Reading 'more than twice' in the wrong order: twice first, then add.
- Forgetting units or answering only x when the question asked for both quantities.
- For perimeter, forgetting the factor 2.

a.text: Shopkeeper: "4 notebooks plus a ₹20 pen cost ₹180." You want the price of one notebook. First step?

a2.text: 180 ÷ 4 = 45, but that includes the pen. Try again with a variable.

choices.label: 4(x + 20) = 180
choices.feedback: That puts a pen with every notebook.

b2.text: There is only one pen. Choose again.

quiz.q: Sum of two numbers is 50; one is 8 more than the other. Smaller number?
quiz.why: If the smaller number is x, the other is x + 8, so 2x + 8 = 50. Then x = 21.

quiz.q: A number when doubled and increased by 9 gives 45. Number?
Perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 54 cm. Side?
quiz.why: The three sides are equal, so 3s = 54 and s = 18 cm.

quiz.q: Each angle at the base of an isosceles triangle is 40°. Vertex angle?
quiz.why: The base angles are 40° each, which is 80° in total. The three angles add to 180°, so the vertex angle is 100°.

quiz.q: Lakshmi is 3 times as old as her son; together 48 years. Son's age?
quiz.why: If the son is x years old, Lakshmi is 3x. Then x + 3x = 48, so x = 12.

questions.q: Which is an equation?
questions.why: An equation has an equals sign with a variable, so 3x − 2 = 10 is an equation. 3x < 10 is an inequality and 3x − 2 is an expression.

questions.q: Solve x − 7 = 0
questions.why: x − 7 = 0 gives x = 7.

questions.q: Solve 8y = 56
"One-fourth of a number is 6" →
questions.why: One-fourth of a number is the number divided by 4, so x/4 = 6.

questions.q: Solve 2x + 5 = −7
Solve 3(p − 2) = 15
Solve m/2 + 3 = 10
Assertion (A): x + 3 = 8 and 2x + 6 = 16 have the same solution. Reason (R): Multiplying both sides by the same non-zero number keeps the solution.
options: Both true, R does not explain A
questions.why: Both are true: x + 3 = 8 gives x = 5, and 2x + 6 = 16 also gives x = 5. Multiplying both sides by 2 keeps the solution, which explains this.

questions.q: Solve 4 = 5(p − 2)
Solve 10 − 3z = −11
Angles of a triangle are x°, 2x° and 3x°. Largest angle?
questions.why: The angles add to 180°, so x + 2x + 3x = 6x = 180 and x = 30. The largest angle is 3x = 90°.

questions.q: Case: A school hall has 180 seats in equal rows of 15, plus x extra chairs, totalling 200. Find x.
questions.why: There are 180 seats plus x extra chairs, so 180 + x = 200 and x = 20.

questions.q: Case: Ravi's monthly pocket money is ₹p. He spends ₹120 and saves one-third of the rest, which is ₹60. Find p.
questions.why: After spending ₹120 he has p − 120, and one-third of that is 60. So p − 120 = 180 and p = 300.

questions.q: Sum of three consecutive multiples of 8 is 888. The largest is
questions.why: Let the multiples be 8x, 8(x + 1) and 8(x + 2). Their sum is 24x + 24 = 888, so x = 36. The largest is 8 × 38 = 304.

questions.q: The perimeter of a rectangle is 64 m; the length is 5 m more than twice the breadth. Length?
questions.why: Let the breadth be b, so the length is 2b + 5. Then 2(b + 2b + 5) = 64, so 6b + 10 = 64 and b = 9. The length is 2(9) + 5 = 23 m.

questions.q: In a bag the number of ₹5 coins is twice the number of ₹10 coins; total value ₹300. Number of ₹10 coins?
questions.why: Let the number of ₹10 coins be n, so there are 2n coins of ₹5. Then 10n + 5(2n) = 300, so 20n = 300 and n = 15.

courses.title: Ch 5 · Lines and Angles
courses.summary: Pairs of angles (complementary, supplementary, adjacent, linear pair, vertically opposite), and the angles made when a transversal cuts two lines, especially parallel lines.
outcomes: Learners can identify and use complementary, supplementary, adjacent and vertically opposite angles
Learners can apply the linear pair property
Learners can name corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles made by a transversal
Learners can use angle facts to find unknown angles and to test whether lines are parallel

scenes.text: A ladder leans on a wall making 65° with the ground. The wall is upright (90° with the ground).
The ladder's angle with the wall plus 65° must make 90°.
So the angle with the wall is 25° — they are complementary angles.

steps.title: Complementary angles
steps.body:
Two angles whose sum is **90°** are complementary. Each is the complement of the other.

- 35° and 55° are complementary.
- Complement of x° is (90 − x)°.

steps.title: Supplementary angles
steps.body:
Two angles whose sum is **180°** are supplementary.

- 110° and 70° are supplementary.
- Supplement of x° is (180 − x)°.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Two complementary angles differ by 20°. Find them.

- Let them be x and x + 20
- x + x + 20 = 90 → 2x = 70 → x = 35
- Angles: **35° and 55°**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
An angle is equal to its supplement. Find it.

- x = 180 − x → 2x = 180 → **x = 90°**

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
Find the angle which is 4 times its complement.

- x = 4(90 − x) → x = 360 − 4x → 5x = 360 → **x = 72°**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Mixing up the two words: think **C**omplementary → **C**orner (90°), **S**upplementary → **S**traight line (180°).
- Thinking two obtuse angles can be supplementary — their sum is more than 180°.

activity.prompt: Match each angle with its complement or supplement.

quiz.why: Complementary angles add up to 90°, so the complement of 72° is 90° − 72° = 18°.
Supplementary angles add up to 180°, so the supplement of 135° is 180° − 135° = 45°.
Two acute angles can be complementary, as their sum can be 90°. They cannot be supplementary, since each is below 90° and the sum is under 180°.

quiz.q: If two angles are supplementary and equal, each is
quiz.why: If two equal angles are supplementary, 2x = 180°, so each is 90°.

quiz.q: An angle is 30° more than its complement. The angle is
quiz.why: If the angle is x, its complement is 90° − x. Then x = 90° − x + 30°, so 2x = 120° and x = 60°.

lessons.title: Adjacent angles, linear pairs, vertically opposite angles

scenes.text: Open a pair of scissors. The blades cross like two lines.
As one angle between the blades grows, the opposite angle grows exactly the same.
These are vertically opposite angles — always equal.

steps.title: Adjacent angles
steps.body: Two angles are adjacent if they have a **common vertex**, a **common arm**, and their other arms lie on **opposite sides** of the common arm (no common interior points).

steps.title: Linear pair
steps.body: A linear pair is a pair of adjacent angles whose non-common arms form a straight line. **Angles of a linear pair add up to 180°** (they are supplementary).

steps.title: Vertically opposite angles
steps.body:
When two lines intersect, they form two pairs of opposite angles. **Vertically opposite angles are equal.**

Why: ∠1 + ∠2 = 180° and ∠2 + ∠3 = 180° (linear pairs), so ∠1 = ∠3.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Two lines cross; one angle is 48°. Find the other three.

- Vertically opposite to 48° → 48°
- Linear pair with 48° → 180 − 48 = 132°
- Its opposite → 132°
- Angles: **48°, 132°, 48°, 132°**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
In a linear pair, one angle is (2x + 10)° and the other is (3x − 5)°. Find x.

- 2x + 10 + 3x − 5 = 180 → 5x + 5 = 180 → **x = 35**
- Angles: 80° and 100°

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Calling any two angles that share a vertex 'adjacent' — they also need a common arm.
- Thinking every supplementary pair is a linear pair. A linear pair must be adjacent.
- Adding vertically opposite angles to get 180°. They are equal, not supplementary.

statements.s: Vertically opposite angles are always equal.
A linear pair can be two acute angles.
statements.why: Two acute angles add to less than 180°.

statements.s: Every pair of supplementary angles forms a linear pair.
Angles of a linear pair are supplementary.
If one angle at an intersection is 90°, all four are 90°.
statements.why: Its opposite is 90° and each neighbour is 180 − 90.

quiz.q: Two lines intersect and one angle is 115°. Its vertically opposite angle is
quiz.why: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the angle opposite 115° is also 115°.

quiz.q: Angles of a linear pair are 3x and 2x. x =
quiz.why: A linear pair adds up to 180°, so 3x + 2x = 5x = 180°, giving x = 36°.
Adjacent angles have a common vertex and a common arm. They need not be equal or add to any fixed total.

quiz.q: Neighbour (adjacent) angle of 70° at an intersection is
quiz.why: The two angles next to each other at an intersection form a linear pair, adding to 180°. So the neighbour of 70° is 110°.

quiz.q: Can a linear pair be 100° and 70°?
quiz.why: A linear pair must add up to 180°. 100° + 70° = 170°, so it is not a linear pair.

lessons.title: Transversals and the angles they make

scenes.text: A straight road crosses two railway tracks at a level crossing.
At each track it makes four angles — eight in all.
Pairs of these angles have special names and, when the tracks are parallel, special relationships.

steps.title: Transversal
steps.body: A line that cuts two or more lines at **distinct points** is a transversal. Cutting two lines, it makes **8 angles**.

steps.title: Names of pairs
steps.body:
Number the angles 1–4 at the top line and 5–8 at the bottom (same positions).

- **Corresponding angles**: same position at each crossing (∠1 & ∠5, ∠2 & ∠6, ∠3 & ∠7, ∠4 & ∠8).
- **Alternate interior angles**: between the lines, on opposite sides of the transversal.
- **Alternate exterior angles**: outside the lines, opposite sides.
- **Interior angles on the same side** (co-interior): between the lines, same side of the transversal.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Line t cuts lines l and m. At l, the angle above l on the right of t is ∠a. Which angle at m corresponds to it?

- The angle above m on the right of t — same position → corresponding to ∠a.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
How many pairs of each kind are formed when a transversal cuts two lines?

- Corresponding: 4 pairs
- Alternate interior: 2 pairs
- Alternate exterior: 2 pairs
- Interior on the same side: 2 pairs

steps.title: Shape trick
steps.body: Corresponding angles sit in an **F** shape, alternate angles in a **Z** shape, co-interior angles in a **C/U** shape.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Calling a line through the intersection point of two lines a transversal — it must cut them at different points.
- Mixing alternate (opposite sides) with co-interior (same side).

activity.prompt: Match the letter shape to the angle pair.
pairs: Interior angles on the same side

quiz.q: A transversal cutting two lines makes how many angles?
quiz.why: A transversal crosses each of the two lines and makes 4 angles at each crossing. So there are 4 + 4 = 8 angles in all.
Alternate interior angles lie between the two lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. They form a Z shape.
Corresponding angles are in the same relative position at the two crossings, such as both above the line and on the left of the transversal. They form an F shape.

quiz.q: How many pairs of corresponding angles?
quiz.why: There are 4 pairs of corresponding angles, one for each of the four positions (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right).

options: the same side, between the lines
quiz.why: Co-interior angles lie between the two lines and on the same side of the transversal. They form a C or U shape.

scenes.text: A carpenter wants two shelf edges to be exactly parallel.
She draws a slanting line across both and measures the corresponding angles.
Both are 62°, so the shelves are parallel. Equal corresponding angles prove it.

steps.title: If the lines are parallel
steps.body:
When a transversal cuts **two parallel lines**:

- each pair of **corresponding angles is equal**
- each pair of **alternate interior angles is equal**
- **interior angles on the same side add up to 180°**

steps.title: Checking for parallel lines (converse)
steps.body:
Two lines cut by a transversal are parallel if any one of these is true:

- a pair of corresponding angles is equal, or
- a pair of alternate interior angles is equal, or
- a pair of co-interior angles is supplementary.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
l ∥ m and a transversal makes ∠1 = 70° at l. Find the corresponding angle, the alternate interior angle and the co-interior angle at m.

- Corresponding = **70°**
- Its linear pair at l = 110°; alternate interior to 70° = **70°**
- Co-interior with 70° = 180 − 70 = **110°**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
Two co-interior angles are (3x + 15)° and (2x + 15)° and the lines are parallel. Find x.

- 3x + 15 + 2x + 15 = 180 → 5x = 150 → **x = 30**
- Angles: 105° and 75°

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
Alternate interior angles are 58° and 62°. Are the lines parallel?

- For parallel lines they must be equal; 58° ≠ 62°
- **Not parallel.**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Using 'corresponding angles are equal' when the lines are not given to be parallel.
- Setting co-interior angles equal instead of adding to 180°.

activity.prompt: l ∥ m. One interior angle on the same side is 47°. Find the other (in degrees).

quiz.q: l ∥ m, corresponding angle is 82°. The other one is
quiz.why: When l ∥ m, corresponding angles are equal. So the other angle is also 82°.

quiz.q: l ∥ m, one co-interior angle 125°. The other is
quiz.why: For parallel lines, co-interior angles add up to 180°. So the other angle is 180° − 125° = 55°.

quiz.q: Alternate interior angles are both 90°. The lines are
quiz.why: If alternate interior angles are equal, the lines are parallel. Both being 90° means they are equal, so the lines are parallel.

quiz.q: If co-interior angles are 100° and 70°, the lines are
quiz.why: Co-interior angles must add to 180° for parallel lines. Since 100° + 70° = 170°, the lines are not parallel.

quiz.q: l ∥ m; alternate interior angles are (4x − 10)° and (2x + 30)°. x =
quiz.why: For parallel lines, alternate interior angles are equal: 4x − 10 = 2x + 30, so 2x = 40 and x = 20.

questions.q: Complement of 25° is
questions.why: The complement of an angle is 90° minus the angle. So 90° − 25° = 65°.

questions.q: Supplement of 90° is
questions.why: The supplement of an angle is 180° minus the angle. So 180° − 90° = 90°.

questions.q: Vertically opposite angles are
questions.why: Vertically opposite angles, formed when two lines cross, are equal.

questions.q: Angles in a linear pair sum to
questions.why: The angles of a linear pair lie on a straight line, so they add up to 180°.

questions.q: Two supplementary angles are in the ratio 2 : 7. The smaller is
questions.why: The ratio 2 : 7 has 9 parts, and the angles add up to 180°. So 1 part is 20° and the smaller angle is 2 × 20° = 40°.

questions.q: When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, alternate interior angles are
questions.why: When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, alternate interior angles are equal.

questions.q: Two lines intersect forming angles x, 3x, x, 3x. x =
questions.why: Two neighbouring angles at an intersection form a linear pair, so x + 3x = 180°. Then 4x = 180° and x = 45°.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Two obtuse angles cannot be supplementary. Reason (R): Each obtuse angle is more than 90°.
options: Both true, R does not explain A
questions.why: Both are true: each obtuse angle is more than 90°, so two obtuse angles add to more than 180°. So they cannot be supplementary.

questions.q: Assertion (A): If corresponding angles are equal, the lines are parallel. Reason (R): Vertically opposite angles are equal.
options: Both true, R does not explain A
questions.why: Both are true: equal corresponding angles mean the lines are parallel, and vertically opposite angles are equal. But the second fact is a different property and does not explain the first.

questions.q: An angle is 24° less than its complement. The angle is
questions.why: Let the angle be x. Its complement is 90° − x, and x is 24° less, so x = 90° − x − 24°. Then 2x = 66° and x = 33°.

questions.q: l ∥ m. A transversal makes an exterior angle of 120° at l. The corresponding angle at m and its vertically opposite angle are
questions.why: For parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal, so the angle at m is 120°. Its vertically opposite angle is also 120°.

questions.q: Case: A road (transversal) crosses two parallel streets. At the first street one angle is 3y and at the second street the co-interior angle is 2y. Find 3y.
questions.why: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°: 3y + 2y = 180°, so y = 36°. Then 3y = 108°.

questions.q: Case: Two mirrors are parallel. A light ray hits the first at an angle of 40° with it and goes on to the second. Angle it makes with the second mirror (alternate)?
questions.why: Alternate interior angles between parallel lines are equal, so the angle with the second mirror is 40°.

questions.q: Lines p and q are cut by a transversal; co-interior angles are (5x − 20)° and (3x + 40)°. For p ∥ q, x =
questions.why: For parallel lines, co-interior angles add to 180°: (5x − 20) + (3x + 40) = 8x + 20 = 180. So 8x = 160 and x = 20.

questions.q: An angle and its supplement differ by 40°. The larger angle is
questions.why: Let the larger angle be x. Its supplement is 180° − x, and the difference is 40°. So x − (180° − x) = 40°, giving 2x = 220° and x = 110°.

questions.q: Of four angles formed at an intersection, one is 4 times its neighbour. The smallest angle is
questions.why: Neighbouring angles at an intersection add to 180°. With one angle x and its neighbour 4x, 5x = 180° and x = 36°, the smallest angle.

courses.title: Ch 6 · The Triangle and its Properties
courses.summary: Medians and altitudes, the exterior angle property, the angle sum property, special triangles, the rule that any two sides add to more than the third, and the Pythagoras property.
outcomes: Learners can draw and describe medians and altitudes
Learners can use the exterior angle and angle sum properties
Learners can decide whether three lengths can make a triangle
Learners can apply the Pythagoras property to right-angled triangles

scenes.text: Meera cuts a triangle from cardboard and tries to balance it on a pencil tip.
She joins each corner to the midpoint of the opposite side — three lines that meet at one point.
It balances exactly there! Those lines are medians.

steps.title: Parts of a triangle
steps.body: A triangle has 3 sides, 3 angles and 3 vertices. Triangles are classified by **sides** (scalene, isosceles, equilateral) and by **angles** (acute, right, obtuse).

steps.title: Median
steps.body: A **median** joins a vertex to the **midpoint of the opposite side**. Every triangle has **3 medians**, and they meet at one point (the centroid), which always lies inside the triangle.

steps.title: Altitude
steps.body:
An **altitude** is the **perpendicular** line segment from a vertex to the opposite side (or the side extended). Every triangle has **3 altitudes**.

- Acute triangle: all altitudes inside.
- Right triangle: two altitudes are the legs themselves.
- Obtuse triangle: two altitudes fall outside.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
In △ABC, D is the midpoint of BC and BC = 10 cm. AD is a median. Find BD.

- D is the midpoint, so BD = DC = 10 ÷ 2 = **5 cm**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
In an isosceles triangle with AB = AC, the median from A to BC is also an altitude. True?

- Yes. In an isosceles triangle the median from the apex is perpendicular to the base. In an equilateral triangle every median is also an altitude.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Drawing the median to any point of the side — it must be the midpoint.
- Drawing the altitude to the midpoint — it must be perpendicular, wherever it lands.
- Thinking altitudes are always inside the triangle.

statements.s: A triangle has exactly 3 medians.
An altitude always lies inside the triangle.
statements.why: In obtuse triangles some altitudes fall outside.

statements.s: Medians meet at a point inside the triangle.
In an equilateral triangle a median is also an altitude.

quiz.q: A median joins a vertex to
options: the midpoint of the opposite side
any point of the opposite side
quiz.why: A median joins a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of the opposite side.

quiz.q: In a right triangle, how many altitudes lie along its sides?
quiz.why: In a right triangle, the two legs are perpendicular to each other, so they are two of the altitudes. So 2 altitudes lie along the sides.
An altitude is the perpendicular line from a vertex to the opposite side. It is not always equal to the median.

quiz.q: Where can an altitude lie outside the triangle?
quiz.why: In an obtuse triangle, the altitudes from the two acute vertices fall outside the triangle. They meet the extended opposite side.

quiz.q: Number of altitudes in a triangle
quiz.why: A triangle has 3 altitudes, one from each vertex.

lessons.title: Exterior angle and angle sum properties

scenes.text: Arnav tears the three corners off a paper triangle.
He places them side by side at one point. They make a straight line!
So the three angles of any triangle add up to 180°.

steps.title: Angle sum property
steps.body:
The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is **180°**: ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°.

Reason: draw a line through A parallel to BC; the alternate angles at A equal ∠B and ∠C, and the three angles at A make a straight angle.

steps.title: Exterior angle property
steps.body:
Extend side BC to D. ∠ACD is an **exterior angle**. It equals the **sum of the two interior opposite angles**:

∠ACD = ∠A + ∠B

So an exterior angle is greater than each interior opposite angle.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
An exterior angle of a triangle is 110° and one interior opposite angle is 45°. Find the other interior opposite angle and the third angle.

- Other opposite angle = 110 − 45 = **65°**
- Interior angle adjacent to the exterior angle = 180 − 110 = **70°**
- Check: 45 + 65 + 70 = 180 ✓

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
Angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find them.

- 9 parts = 180 → 1 part = 20
- **40°, 60°, 80°**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Adding the adjacent interior angle to find the exterior angle — use the two *opposite* interior angles.
- Believing a triangle can have two right angles (that would already be 180°).

activity.prompt: In △ABC, ∠A = 3x, ∠B = 2x, ∠C = 4x. Find x (degrees).

quiz.q: Two angles of a triangle are 90° and 30°. The third is
quiz.why: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°, so the third angle is 180° − (90° + 30°) = 60°.

quiz.q: An exterior angle is 130°; the interior opposite angles are equal. Each is
quiz.why: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles. If they are equal, each is 130° ÷ 2 = 65°.
The angles of a triangle must add up to 180°. 100° + 50° + 40° = 190°, so no.

quiz.q: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is
quiz.why: The three angles of an equilateral triangle are equal and add to 180°, so each is 60°.

quiz.q: In a right triangle, one acute angle is 35°. The other is
quiz.why: In a right triangle the two acute angles add to 90°, so the other angle is 90° − 35° = 55°.

lessons.title: Special triangles and the sum of two sides

scenes.text: Kavya has sticks of 3 cm, 4 cm and 9 cm. She cannot make a triangle!
3 + 4 = 7, which is shorter than 9 — the short sticks cannot reach.
With 5 cm, 6 cm, 9 cm it works, because 5 + 6 > 9.

steps.title: Equilateral and isosceles
steps.body:
- **Equilateral**: all sides equal, each angle 60°.
- **Isosceles**: two sides equal; the angles opposite the equal sides (base angles) are equal.

steps.title: Triangle inequality
steps.body:
The **sum of the lengths of any two sides is greater than the third side**. Also, the difference of any two sides is less than the third.

Quick test: check that the two shorter sides add to more than the longest.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Can 2.5 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm form a triangle?

- Two shorter: 2.5 + 4 = 6.5 < 7
- **No.**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
Two sides of a triangle are 8 cm and 13 cm. Between which lengths must the third side lie?

- Greater than 13 − 8 = 5 and less than 13 + 8 = 21
- **5 cm < third side < 21 cm**

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
In an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle is 40°. Find each base angle.

- 2x + 40 = 180 → x = **70°**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Testing only one pair of sides. If you do not order them, test all three pairs.
- Allowing equality: 3, 4, 7 does not make a triangle because 3 + 4 = 7 (it is flat).

activity.prompt: Can these lengths form a triangle?

quiz.why: In a triangle, the sum of two sides must be greater than the third. 5 + 7 = 12, which is less than 13, so no triangle is possible.

quiz.q: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are 55° each. Vertex angle?
quiz.why: The base angles add to 110°, so the vertex angle is 180° − 110° = 70°.

quiz.q: Two sides are 6 cm and 9 cm. Third side could be
quiz.why: The third side must be greater than 9 − 6 = 3 and less than 9 + 6 = 15. So 10 cm is possible, but 2, 3 and 16 are not.

quiz.q: In an equilateral triangle, each exterior angle is
quiz.why: Each interior angle is 60°, so each exterior angle is 180° − 60° = 120°.

quiz.q: The difference of two sides of a triangle is
quiz.why: The difference of two sides of a triangle is less than the third side. This follows from the triangle inequality.

lessons.title: Right-angled triangles and the Pythagoras property

scenes.text: A kite is 12 m above the ground, directly above a point 5 m from Rohan.
How long is the tight string? It is the hypotenuse of a right triangle.
5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13². The string is 13 m long.

steps.title: The property
steps.body:
In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite the right angle is the **hypotenuse** (longest side); the other two are the **legs**.

**Pythagoras property: (hypotenuse)² = (leg)² + (leg)²**

If a² + b² = c² for three lengths, the triangle is right-angled with the right angle opposite c (converse). Such whole numbers are called **Pythagorean triplets**: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (6, 8, 10), (8, 15, 17).

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the hypotenuse.

- h² = 36 + 64 = 100
- h = **10 cm**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
A 15 m ladder reaches a window 12 m high. How far is its foot from the wall?

- d² + 12² = 15² → d² = 225 − 144 = 81
- d = **9 m**

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
Is a triangle with sides 7 cm, 24 cm, 25 cm right-angled?

- 7² + 24² = 49 + 576 = 625 = 25²
- **Yes**, right angle opposite the 25 cm side.

steps.title: Solved example 4
steps.body:
Find the diagonal of a rectangle 40 cm × 30 cm.

- d² = 1600 + 900 = 2500 → d = **50 cm**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Adding the hypotenuse squared to a leg squared. The hypotenuse is always alone on one side.
- Forgetting the square root at the end (writing 100 instead of 10).
- Using the property in a triangle that is not right-angled.

activity.prompt: Hypotenuse 17 cm, one leg 8 cm. Find the other leg.

quiz.why: A Pythagorean triplet satisfies a² + b² = c². 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13².
By Pythagoras, hypotenuse² = 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, so the hypotenuse is 15.

quiz.q: The longest side of a right triangle is
quiz.why: The longest side of a right triangle is the hypotenuse, which is opposite the 90° angle.

quiz.q: A tree breaks 5 m above ground and its top touches the ground 12 m from the base. Original height?
quiz.why: The broken part is the hypotenuse of a triangle with sides 5 and 12, so it is √(25 + 144) = 13 m. The original height is 5 + 13 = 18 m.
1.5² + 2² = 2.25 + 4 = 6.25 = 2.5², so the sides satisfy Pythagoras. It is a right triangle.

questions.q: Sum of angles of a triangle is
questions.why: The three angles of any triangle add up to 180°. This is the angle sum property.

questions.q: A median joins a vertex to
questions.why: A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

questions.q: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is
questions.why: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle, and it is the longest side.

questions.q: Two angles are 70° and 60°. Third angle?
questions.why: The third angle is 180° − (70° + 60°) = 50°.

questions.q: An exterior angle is 125° and one interior opposite angle is 60°. The other is
questions.why: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles. So the other angle is 125° − 60° = 65°.

questions.q: Can 4 cm, 8 cm, 12 cm make a triangle?
questions.why: The sum of two sides must be greater than the third. 4 + 8 = 12, which is not greater than 12, so no triangle is possible.

questions.q: Legs 20 and 21. Hypotenuse?
questions.why: Hypotenuse² = 20² + 21² = 400 + 441 = 841, and 29² = 841. So the hypotenuse is 29.

questions.q: Assertion (A): A triangle can have two obtuse angles. Reason (R): The angle sum of a triangle is 180°.
questions.why: The assertion is false: two obtuse angles would add to more than 180°, so a triangle cannot have two. The reason is true, that the angle sum is 180°.

questions.q: Assertion (A): 8, 15, 17 form a right triangle. Reason (R): 8² + 15² = 17².
options: Both true, R does not explain A
questions.why: Both are true: 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17². This is why 8, 15, 17 form a right triangle.

questions.q: Angles of a triangle are x, x + 10, x + 20. Largest angle?
questions.why: The angles add to 180°: x + (x + 10) + (x + 20) = 3x + 30 = 180, so x = 50. The largest angle is 50 + 20 = 70°.

questions.q: Each base angle of an isosceles triangle is twice the vertex angle. The vertex angle is
questions.why: Let the vertex angle be x, so each base angle is 2x. Then x + 2x + 2x = 180°, so 5x = 180° and x = 36°.

questions.q: Case: A 26 m rope is tied from the top of a 24 m pole to a peg on the ground. Distance of the peg from the foot of the pole?
questions.why: The rope is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the pole. Distance² = 26² − 24² = 676 − 576 = 100, so the distance is 10 m.

questions.q: Case: A rhombus has diagonals 16 cm and 30 cm (they bisect each other at right angles). Side of the rhombus?
questions.why: The half-diagonals are 8 and 15 cm and meet at right angles, so the side is √(64 + 225) = √289 = 17 cm.

questions.q: Two sides of a triangle are 12 cm and 7 cm. How many whole-number lengths are possible for the third side?
questions.why: The third side must be greater than 12 − 7 = 5 and less than 12 + 7 = 19. The whole numbers 6 to 18 work, which is 13 values.

questions.q: In △ABC, ∠A = 2∠B and the exterior angle at C is 105°. ∠B =
questions.why: The exterior angle at C equals ∠A + ∠B = 2∠B + ∠B = 3∠B = 105°. So ∠B = 35°.

questions.q: Two poles of heights 6 m and 11 m stand 12 m apart on level ground. Distance between their tops?
questions.why: The difference in heights is 11 − 6 = 5 m and the poles are 12 m apart, so the distance between the tops is √(25 + 144) = 13 m.

courses.title: Ch 7 · Comparing Quantities
courses.summary: Ratios and equivalent ratios, percentages and converting between fractions, decimals and percents, percentage increase and decrease, profit and loss, and simple interest.
outcomes: Learners can compare quantities using ratios and percentages
Learners can convert between fractions, decimals and percentages
Learners can calculate profit, loss and their percentages
Learners can compute simple interest and amount

scenes.text: A painter mixes 2 tins of white with 3 tins of blue to get sky blue.
For a bigger wall she needs 15 tins of blue. How much white?
2 : 3 = x : 15 → x = 10 tins. Keeping the ratio keeps the colour.

steps.title: Ratio
steps.body:
A **ratio** compares two quantities of the **same kind in the same units** by division. a : b = a/b. Ratios have no unit.

Example: 50 cm to 2 m → 50 cm : 200 cm = 1 : 4.

steps.title: Equivalent ratios and proportion
steps.body:
Multiplying or dividing both terms by the same non-zero number gives an **equivalent ratio**: 3 : 4 = 6 : 8 = 15 : 20.

Four numbers are in **proportion** if a : b = c : d, i.e. a × d = b × c.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Are 1 : 2 and 2 : 3 equivalent?

- 1/2 = 0.5, 2/3 ≈ 0.67
- **Not equivalent.**

steps.title: Solved example 2 (unitary method)
steps.body:
6 bowls cost ₹90. Cost of 10 bowls?

- 1 bowl = 90 ÷ 6 = ₹15
- 10 bowls = **₹150**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Comparing quantities in different units (50 paise to ₹1 is 50 : 100, not 50 : 1).
- Reversing the order: boys to girls is not the same as girls to boys.

activity.prompt: Match each ratio to its simplest form.

quiz.why: 3 km = 3000 m, so the ratio is 3000 : 300 = 10 : 1.
Multiplying both parts of 5 : 7 by 3 gives 15 : 21, and by 5 gives 25 : 35. Both are equivalent ratios.
One pen costs 96 ÷ 8 = ₹12, so 5 pens cost 5 × 12 = ₹60.
A ratio compares two quantities of the same unit, so the units cancel. A ratio has no units.

scenes.text: Sana got 18/25 in Maths and 32/40 in Science.
Different totals make comparing hard.
Maths 72%, Science 80%. Percent means "per hundred" — a common scale.

steps.title: Meaning of percent
steps.body: **Percent (%) means per hundred.** 35% = 35/100 = 0.35.

steps.title: Converting
steps.body:
- Fraction → %: multiply by 100. 3/8 × 100 = 37.5%
- Decimal → %: multiply by 100. 0.06 = 6%
- % → fraction: divide by 100 and simplify. 45% = 45/100 = 9/20
- % → decimal: 12.5% = 0.125

steps.title: Percent of a quantity
steps.body:
x% of Q = (x/100) × Q. 25% of 360 = 90.

Finding the whole: if 20% of a number is 14, number = 14 × 100/20 = 70.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
In a class of 40, 16 are girls. What percent are boys?

- Boys = 24
- 24/40 × 100 = **60%**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
A school team won 60% of its matches and won 15. How many matches did it play?

- 60% of n = 15 → n = 15 × 100/60 = **25 matches**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Writing 0.5 = 5%. It is 50%.
- Adding percentages of different wholes (40% of class A + 30% of class B ≠ 70% of everyone).
- Forgetting that the parts must total 100%.

activity.prompt: Convert.
activity.text: 3/4 = ___%,  0.08 = ___%,  12% as a fraction in lowest terms = ___

quiz.why: To change a decimal to a percent, multiply by 100: 0.375 × 100 = 37.5%.
If 25% (a quarter) of x is 40, then x = 40 × 4 = 160.

quiz.q: In a fruit basket 30% are apples. Percent not apples?
quiz.why: If 30% are apples, the rest are 100% − 30% = 70%.

scenes.text: Kabir buys cupcakes for ₹400 and sells them all for ₹500.
Profit = ₹100. As a percent of what he spent: 100/400 × 100 = 25%.
Next year he wants a 30% profit. He will need to sell for ₹520.

steps.title: Increase and decrease
steps.body:
Percentage change = (change ÷ original value) × 100.

- Price ₹50 → ₹60: increase 10/50 × 100 = 20%
- Always divide by the **original** value.

steps.title: Profit and loss
steps.body:
- **CP** = cost price, **SP** = selling price.
- SP > CP → Profit = SP − CP
- CP > SP → Loss = CP − SP
- Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100; Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100
- Overhead expenses (transport, repair) are added to CP.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
A cycle bought for ₹2500 is sold for ₹2150. Find loss %.

- Loss = 2500 − 2150 = 350
- Loss % = 350/2500 × 100 = **14%**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
An item costs ₹800. Find SP for 15% profit.

- Profit = 15% of 800 = 120
- SP = 800 + 120 = **₹920**

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
Juhi sells a washing machine for ₹13 500 with a 20% loss. Find the CP.

- SP = 80% of CP → CP = 13 500 × 100/80 = **₹16 875**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Computing profit % on SP. It is always on CP (unless told otherwise).
- Forgetting overhead expenses in CP.
- A 10% increase then 10% decrease does NOT bring you back: 100 → 110 → 99.

activity.prompt: A TV bought for ₹12 000 is sold for ₹13 800. Profit percent?

quiz.why: The increase is ₹10 on an original ₹40, so the increase is 10/40 × 100 = 25%.
Profit and loss percentages are calculated on the cost price (CP).

quiz.q: Bought for ₹4500, spent ₹500 on repairs, sold for ₹5500. Profit %?

scenes.text: Leela borrows ₹10 000 from a bank at 8% per year to buy a sewing machine.
After 3 years she must repay the loan plus interest.

steps.title: Words to know
steps.body:
- **Principal (P)**: money borrowed or deposited.
- **Rate (R)**: interest % per year (per annum).
- **Time (T)**: in years.
- **Interest**: extra money paid for using money.
- **Amount (A)** = P + SI.

steps.title: Formula
steps.body:
**SI = (P × R × T) / 100**

Rearranged: P = 100 × SI/(R × T), R = 100 × SI/(P × T), T = 100 × SI/(P × R).

If time is in months, convert: 6 months = ½ year.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
In how many years will ₹2000 earn ₹480 interest at 8% p.a.?

- T = 100 × 480 / (2000 × 8) = 48000/16000 = **3 years**

steps.title: Solved example 3
steps.body:
At what rate will ₹4000 become ₹5000 in 5 years?

- SI = 1000
- R = 100 × 1000 / (4000 × 5) = **5% p.a.**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Using months directly in the formula as years.
- Giving SI when asked for amount (or the reverse).
- Forgetting to divide by 100.

activity.prompt: Simple interest on ₹15 000 at 10% p.a. for 2 years (₹)

quiz.why: Amount = principal + interest = 800 + 96 = ₹896.
6 months is 6/12 of a year, which is 1/2 year.

quiz.q: Money doubles in 10 years at simple interest. Rate?
quiz.why: If the money doubles, SI equals the principal. So P = P × R × 10/100, giving R = 10%.

questions.q: Ratio 50 paise : ₹1
questions.why: ₹1 = 100 paise, so the ratio is 50 : 100 = 1 : 2.

questions.q: 1/4 as a percent
SP > CP means
questions.why: When SP is more than CP, there is a profit. If SP is less, there is a loss.

questions.q: Price ₹80 reduced by 15%. New price?
questions.why: The reduction is 15% of ₹80 = ₹12, so the new price is 80 − 12 = ₹68.

questions.q: SI on ₹2500 at 4% for 3 years
Assertion (A): A 20% rise followed by a 20% fall gives the original price. Reason (R): Percent change is measured from the current value each time.
questions.why: The assertion is false: a 20% rise makes 100 into 120, and a 20% fall of 120 is 24, giving 96, not 100. The reason is true, since each percent is taken on the current value.

questions.q: CP of 12 pencils = SP of 10 pencils. Profit %?
questions.why: If CP of 12 pencils equals SP of 10 pencils, the SP of one pencil is 12/10 = 1.2 times its CP. So the profit is 20%.

questions.q: A sells for ₹1140 at a 5% loss. CP?
questions.why: A 5% loss means SP is 95% of CP. So CP = 1140 ÷ 0.95 = ₹1200.

questions.q: At what rate does ₹6000 earn ₹1080 in 3 years?
Case: A shop marks a shirt at ₹1200 and gives 10% off; the shirt cost the shop ₹900. Profit %?
Case: A town of 25 000 people grows by 4% this year. Population next year?
questions.why: A 4% growth gives 25 000 × 1.04 = 26 000 people.

questions.q: Two items of ₹500 each: one sold at 10% profit, one at 10% loss. Overall?
questions.why: At 10% profit the SP is ₹550, and at 10% loss it is ₹450. The total SP is ₹1000, which equals the total CP, so there is no profit and no loss.

questions.q: A sum amounts to ₹7200 in 2 years and ₹8100 in 3 years at simple interest. Principal?
questions.why: The amount rose by 8100 − 7200 = ₹900 in one year, so SI per year is ₹900. For 2 years SI is ₹1800, so P = 7200 − 1800 = ₹5400.

questions.q: In what time will ₹1500 amount to ₹1800 at 4% p.a. simple interest?

courses.title: Ch 8 · Rational Numbers
